Consumers must know which they have.

findings.title: Error message logs the awaited module object instead of the app type string
findings.body: Line 591: `console.warn(`payment App service of type ${paymentApp} is not implemented`);` — `paymentApp` is now the awaited module namespace object (or undefined), not a string. Previously it was also the module object (the old code had the same bug: `appStore[...]` returned a module namespace), so this is a pre-existing defect, but the PR touches this line's context. The message will print something like 'payment App service of type [object Module] is not implemented' or 'undefined', which is useless for debugging. It should log `paymentAppCredential?.app?.dirName` (the intended app identifier) instead. Same pattern exists in packages/lib/payment/deletePayment.ts line 18 and packages/lib/payment/handlePayment.ts line 28 and packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx line 969 — all log `${paymentApp}` which is a module object.

findings.title: Comment 'example: import("./example")' references a non-existent example app and is misleading
findings.body: Line 2: `// example: import("./example"),` — the commented-out example references `./example` which does not exist in the app-store directory (the actual example app is `_example`). The comment is meant to show the pattern for adding a new app, but as written it would mislead a developer into uncommenting a broken import. It should reference `./_example` or be removed. Minor, but it's the only documentation of how to add an app to this store.

findings.title: getCalendar(calendarCredential) may return null and calendar?.deleteEvent is called with a possibly-null credential result; also the await is inside a block that previously relied on synchronous behavior
findings.body: Line 483-489: `const calendarCredential = await prisma.credential.findUnique({...}); const calendar = await getCalendar(calendarCredential); await calendar?.deleteEvent(oldCalendarEvent.uid, event, oldCalendarEvent.externalCalendarId);`. getCalendar returns null if credential is null or has no key — the optional chaining handles that. But note that `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` returns a Promise that is awaited — fine. However, this whole block is inside the `if (newBookingId)` merge path of updateAllCalendarEvents, which is wrapped in a try/catch that returns a synthetic failure result. If the dynamic import inside getCalendar rejects (broken app), the catch at line 516 handles it and returns a failure EventResult — acceptable. The main concern is consistency: this is one of the few places that correctly awaits, showing the pattern the other files should follow. No change needed here, but it confirms the forEach/forEach-async bugs elsewhere are deviations from the intended pattern.

findings.title: Reschedule cleanup in handleNewBooking pushes deleteEvent promises into integrationsToDelete but the surrounding loop may not await getCalendar before pushing
findings.body: The diff shows `const calendar = await getCalendar(credential);` inside what appears to be a for...of or forEach loop around line 885-890. The snippet shows `integrationsToDelete.push(calendar?.deleteEvent(reference.uid, originalBookingEvt, reference.externalCalendarId))`. If this is inside a `forEach` (as the vital/wipemycalother reschedule files do), the await inside a non-async forEach callback would be a syntax error — so it must be a for...of or an async forEach. Given the diff context (`integrationsToDelete.push(deleteMeeting(credential, reference.uid));` on the line before, also without await on deleteMeeting which is fine since it returns a promise), the structure appears to be a for...of loop. However, the file was only shown as 'diff only' — the full context of whether integrationsToDelete promises are awaited before the new booking is confirmed is not visible. If they are awaited via Promise.all later, this is fine; if not, the same orphaned-event race as the other files applies. Flagging for verification: ensure `await Promise.all(integrationsToDelete)` occurs before the handler returns success, otherwise old calendar/video events from the original booking may outlive the rescheduled booking.
